cases.expected_contract: Pins AppendFile as the same ordered trace with the opposite flag. The decisive row is the EMPTY append: the pin leaves the file at six bytes, where any implementation that opened with O_TRUNC and wrote only the new content would leave it at zero. The external truncate between two appends pins that the offset is the kernel's and not the caller's -- the next append starts at zero, not at six -- which is the property O_APPEND buys and a read-modify-write port does not have. Creation of a missing file and of a missing parent are both pinned, the latter being the row that reaches ensureDirectoryExists. Appending onto a directory fails with is_a_directory after the ensure layer has run, and the relative literal panics at the rootedness assert before the bottom layer is entered.
cases.host_applicability: posix, non-root: both active native targets run these paths, but the results recorded here are darwin/arm64's and do not certify linux
cases.native_authority: tools/phase1/filesystem probes against the pinned packages

cases.expected_contract: The lost-timestamp-argument control. Both stamps are read back after every call as separate SECONDS and NANOSECONDS, never as a clock reading: the first call sets two distinct constants and the row records both, so a port that passed one argument twice, or derived one from the other, fails on the first row. The next three rows pin the zero-value contract, which os/file_posix.go:188-200 implements as UTIME_OMIT: zero for the access time leaves the access time alone while the modification time moves, zero for the modification time does the reverse, and zero for both is a no-op rather than a touch. The precision row records what nanosecond remainder the filesystem KEPT of a value the probe chose, which is how the plan's precision-not-sleeping requirement is met; this host keeps all nine digits. A directory is accepted, a symlink is FOLLOWED (the target's stamps move, the link's own do not, read through lstat), and a missing path is a *PathError with Op "chtimes". The last two rows pin the representable range: 2200 round-trips and 2500 comes back negative, because the conversion goes through Time.UnixNano. The relative literal reaches Chtimes and fails with not_exist, which is how the case records that this method has no rootedness assert without mutating anything outside its root. times_class and link_times read the raw stat and reach nothing.
cases.host_applicability: host-specific: timestamp resolution is a filesystem property, not a language one. This darwin/APFS host keeps the full nanosecond remainder; an ext4 host with a small inode, or a FAT volume, keeps less, and the precision row is what says so rather than the case failing.
cases.native_authority: tools/phase1/filesystem probes against the pinned packages

cases.expected_contract: Pins the directory layer directly: one level, three levels in one call, an ALREADY EXISTING directory (which must return nil and must NOT have its 0o700 mode changed to 0o777), a path whose component is a regular file, a path under a read-only parent, a symlink to a directory, and the root itself. The created mode is recorded beside the process umask so 0o755 is readable as 0o777 masked, and the existing-directory row is the one that catches a port that chmods what it finds. The final row hands it a RELATIVE path from inside the per-case root, which is the only way to see that this layer has no rootedness assert -- the assert lives one layer up, and that asymmetry is the reason writeFileEnsuringDir exists as a separate function. The mkdir, chmod, write_file_raw and symlink rows are setup through the os package and reach nothing pinned.
cases.host_applicability: posix, non-root: both active native targets run these paths, but the results recorded here are darwin/arm64's and do not certify linux

cases.expected_contract: Pins both predicates on the same path in the same row, because they are one contract: each is Stat plus a test of IsDir, so a port that changed the underlying lookup flips them together and a port that changed only one is visible immediately. The decisive fixture is the FIFO, which answers FileExists TRUE and DirectoryExists false: Go's predicate is `!IsDir()` while Rust's is_file() means REGULAR file, and no regular-file fixture can find that. The symlink trio (to a file, to a directory, dangling) separates stat from lstat, the denied directory and the path inside it separate 'answer false' from 'propagate a permission error', and the root with and without a trailing slash pins that SplitPath removes it. The last action asks the same path twice with a real removal in between, which is the cache check; it uses os.Remove for the mutation and so reaches FileExists only.

cases.expected_contract: Pins that FS() hands back ONE live host, not a snapshot and not a fresh object. Two handles are acquired and the second acquisition records that it is the same value as the first; then every write through one handle is read back through the other, in both directions. A snapshot port -- the only OS-aware shape crates/tsr_vfs offers -- answers the pre-mutation bytes and fails at the first cross-handle read. The entries row adds the same property for directory listing: a symlink created after both handles existed appears in the first handle's listing. The writes reach all three write layers, because WriteFile is writeFileEnsuringDir is writeFileWithFlag; they do NOT reach ensureDirectoryExists, since the parent exists and the first attempt succeeds. The symlink row is setup through os.Symlink and reaches nothing pinned, and GetAccessibleEntries does not reach isReparsePoint here because no entry is ModeIrregular on a posix host.

cases.expected_contract: Reproduces the pinned fixture of realpath_test.go:106-151 -- a directory of four symlinks beside the link-free directory they point at -- and extends it with the three entry kinds that test never creates. Each row records the Files list, the Directories list, the SORTED symlink set, whether that set is non-nil, and the three lengths. Files and Directories are SORTED BY NAME, which is the contract: internal.go:123 calls io/fs.ReadDir, os.DirFS satisfies fs.ReadDirFS, and its ReadDir goes through os.ReadDir, which sorts (os/dir.go:122-124). The symlink set is a Go map and is sorted by the probe before it is recorded, since map order is randomised and is not the contract. The two decisive extensions are a DANGLING symlink and a FIFO, both of which the pin drops from all three lists (internal.go:71-83 admits only IsDir or IsRegular, and internal.go:95 drops an entry whose follow-up Stat is nil), and a HARD link, which is a plain file and not a symlink. Four inputs -- missing, denied, a regular file and an unrooted root form -- all answer empty lists with a NON-NIL empty symlink set, which vfs.go:55-60 makes a different answer from nil.
cases.host_applicability: posix, non-root: both active native targets run these paths, but the results recorded here are darwin/arm64's and do not certify linux

cases.expected_contract: Pins the composed location as a DECOMPOSITION, never as a path: its leading component is the host's user cache directory, which names a home directory. The row records whether the result is nonempty and absolute, whether the user cache lookup succeeded, whether the result starts with that cache directory, whether it instead starts with the temporary directory (the fallback branch, which must be false when the lookup succeeded), that it contains no backslash and no doubled slash, the middle component, the last component and the component count. The middle component is "typescript" on a posix host and "Microsoft/TypeScript" on windows, so the is_windows predicate travels in its own provenance `host` row -- as a predicate and not as runtime.GOOS, whose literal spelling is Go's own platform vocabulary and is not reproducible by a Rust port. The last component is the MAJOR.MINOR version and the expected suffix travels in the request, which is the only row that separates a port appending core.VersionMajorMinor() from one appending the full 7.1.0-dev. Two calls are compared to each other because the pin recomputes rather than caching and must be stable. The Rust side is a recorded gap rather than an observation: the only similarly named Rust method returns an empty string by design and is not a port of this.
cases.host_applicability: host-specific: the leading component is the host's user cache directory -- $HOME/Library/Caches on this darwin host, $XDG_CACHE_HOME or $HOME/.cache on linux -- so only the decomposition is recorded and never the path. The middle component also differs by platform (os.go:237-241), which is why the `host` row travels beside it, recording the is_windows predicate rather than runtime.GOOS.

cases.expected_contract: Calls both entry points on every input and records the pair plus whether they agree, because osvfs.isReparsePoint is nativepath.IsSymlinkOrReparsePoint after filepath.FromSlash and on a posix host that translation is the identity. Eleven inputs cover a real directory, a real file, a symlink to each, a DANGLING symlink, a hard link, a FIFO, a missing path, a 0o000 directory, the root itself, and a symlink whose own NAME contains a backslash. The dangling one is the input that cannot be passed by accident: Lstat succeeds on the link itself so the pin answers TRUE, while any implementation built on metadata or exists answers false or errors. The missing and empty-string inputs pin that an Lstat error becomes false rather than propagating -- the caller at internal.go:105 has no error channel. The backslash name is what makes the FromSlash layer observable on posix at all. No action reaches GetAccessibleEntries: on this host no directory entry is ModeIrregular, so the pin's one production call site of isReparsePoint is unreachable and the predicate is driven directly.
cases.host_applicability: posix: symlink_other.go is //go:build !windows, so these rows certify the posix arm only. The windows arm (GetFileAttributesEx and FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT, which also answers true for a junction) is a different operation id and is not reached here.

cases.expected_contract: Pins the !windows && !linux build of nativepath.Realpath directly, where its caller cannot: osFSRealpath discards the error entirely, so the error IDENTITY -- the one thing that distinguishes the two builds -- is invisible from above. Measured here: a dangling link and a missing path both give a *PathError with Op "lstat", and a symlink CYCLE gives a bare *errors.errorString, not a *PathError at all, so a port that modelled every failure as one type cannot reproduce the pair. The relative row is the other half of the composition's reason for existing: a relative input stays RELATIVE here, which is why osFSRealpath calls filepath.Abs afterwards. It is the only action in this group that moves the process working directory, and it restores it immediately. The long row builds a path past 256 resolved bytes, which is an ordinary long path on this build and the buffer-doubling loop on the linux one. The `build` row is provenance: it records the single predicate `GOOS == "linux"`, which is exactly the build constraint that selects realpath_linux.go over realpath_other.go, so the error rows can be attributed to the right file. runtime.GOOS itself is not recorded -- its spelling is Go's own and carries nothing a port can match.
cases.host_applicability: host-specific: darwin (and any !windows && !linux). On linux this row set is recorded as native_unavailable, because the pinned file is not compiled there.
cases.native_authority: tools/phase1/filesystem probes against the pinned packages

cases.expected_contract: The same trace, gated to linux, where nativepath.Realpath is the procfs implementation rather than per-component evaluation. On THIS capture it is recorded as native_unavailable with the build constraint as the reason, and it is deliberately NOT answered with the darwin build's results: the two implementations differ in exactly the way this case exists to record, so substituting one for the other would certify nothing. On a linux host the same rows witness a *PathError with Op "open" where the other build says "lstat", a possible Op "readlink" that the other build never produces, and the buffer-doubling loop at realpath_linux.go:65-68 on the long input. Those rows would also pass through nativepath.ignoringEINTR, which this capture cannot reach and which is reported unreached rather than claimed here, because the only arm a caller can drive is the no-error pass-through and its retry semantics need a probe-supplied closure from inside package nativepath. It also reaches eintr_unix.go:ignoringEINTR, which is unexported and //go:build linux and has no other caller: realpath_linux.go:44 and :59 are both inside Realpath's own body, so any run that observes Realpath on linux observes the retry wrapper with it. On this darwin capture the whole row is native_unavailable and neither operation is observed; a linux capture is what certifies them.
cases.host_applicability: host-specific: linux only, by realpath_linux.go having no build constraint while realpath_other.go excludes linux. On this darwin capture the row is native_unavailable and is NOT replaced by the darwin answer: one host's results never certify the other.

cases.expected_contract: The Go and Rust probes are separate processes, so record classes rather than literal executable paths or argv. Args reports (has an argument, argv[0] nonempty, raw native argv forwarded unchanged). Executable reports (no error, absolute, exists, basename nonempty, resolves successfully to the same OS file, raw native executable path forwarded unchanged), before and after chdir. The final resolution observation is [resolution_succeeded, same_file_identity, raw_path_forwarded]. The earlier equality of raw versus resolved path spelling was removed on 2026-09-22: on Darwin the Go temporary launch path may use /var while the workspace Rust binary uses /private/var, even though both forward the same _NSGetExecutablePath primitive faithfully. The native probe uses os.SameFile and the Rust probe uses dev/ino, so this no longer grades test-process placement. Both exported osutil functions reach their non-Android unexported delegates. Only executable_class invokes nativepath.Realpath.
cases.host_applicability: POSIX. The class comparison permits platform-specific executable path spelling; the same-file check must succeed on the active native build. This Darwin capture does not certify Linux procfs resolution or Android executable/argv behavior.
cases.native_authority: tools/phase1/filesystem probes against the pinned packages

cases.expected_contract: Pins ReadFile's full decoding contract as (contents_hex, ok, length) per fixture. Hex is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: the invalid-UTF-8 fixture comes back as the raw bytes ff41, which cannot survive encoding/json in either direction, and the same representation makes the UTF-16 rows readable. The trap the case is built around is that FOUR different files answer ("", true) -- an empty file, a bare UTF-8 BOM, a bare UTF-16 BOM and a two-byte-BOM file -- while a missing file, a directory, a dangling symlink, a denied file and a path inside a denied directory all answer ("", false). Only the boolean separates the two groups, which is exactly what a port is most likely to collapse. The literal rows add the rootedness assert (the pinned panic text) and two non-posix root forms that are rooted to tspath and simply miss. The write_bytes and chmod actions are setup through os.WriteFile and os.Chmod and reach nothing pinned.
cases.host_applicability: posix, non-root: both active native targets run these paths, but the results recorded here are darwin/arm64's and do not certify linux

cases.expected_contract: Pins the resolving half of Realpath through the exported method, which is the semaphore wrapper around osFSRealpath, which is filepath.EvalSymlinks on this build -- so every row reaches all three operations. It reproduces the pinned assertion of realpath_test.go:13-33 (a file and the same file through a directory symlink resolve to the same string), then a three-deep symlink chain, the root itself, and a symlink that points at the root. Results are recorded relative to <root> or <realroot> and never as paths: this host reaches its temporary root through /var -> /private/var, so the resolved spelling differs from the spelling handed in, and that difference is the point. The case-swapped row is the measured divergence: TARGET/FILE resolves to <realroot>/TARGET/FILE, the spelling given, where std::fs::canonicalize returns the on-disk casing. The last row removes the target between two calls and shows the answer fall back to the UNRESOLVED input, which is the fallback contract seen from the resolving side. remembered_count is a bookkeeping row and reaches nothing.
cases.host_applicability: host-specific: the resolved spelling is the host's. This darwin host resolves the temporary root through /var -> /private/var, which is why every row is recorded relative to <root> or <realroot> rather than as a path; the case-swap row is valid only on a case-insensitive volume and records that volume's answer

cases.expected_contract: Pins the half of osFSRealpath that has no error channel. Three on-disk failures -- a dangling symlink, a missing path and a symlink cycle -- each return the input UNTOUCHED, recorded as equals_input alongside the placed path, and one success is included as the control so 'returns its input' is not trivially true. Five root forms that tspath roots and the host does not understand (a DOS root, a UNC root, an untitled root and two URL roots) go through the same branch: they do not panic, because GetEncodedRootLength gives each of them a root, and they come back unchanged. The relative spelling is the one that DOES panic, with internal.RootLength's literal text, and the probe supplies that path itself so the quoted string in the recorded text is portable. Most rows call the unexported composition directly so the assert and the fallbacks are visible without the semaphore; one row repeats a failure through the exported method to show the wrapper changes nothing.
cases.host_applicability: host-specific for the three on-disk rows; the five root-form rows are host-independent on any posix host, and windows would differ because filepath.FromSlash is not the identity there

cases.expected_contract: Pins Remove as os.RemoveAll semantics with the four properties a port is most likely to get wrong, each with a SURVIVOR check in the same row. A missing path returns nil rather than an error. A populated nested tree is removed recursively. A symlink to a file and a symlink to a directory are both removed WITHOUT touching their targets, which the survivor list records explicitly because getting this wrong deletes a user's real directory. A hard link survives the removal of the file it shares an inode with. A FIFO and a dangling symlink are removed like anything else. The two 0o000 rows pin PARTIAL removal: the call returns a permission error and the tree is left half-deleted, and after the mode is restored the same call succeeds. The empty-path row is the ONLY non-rooted spelling this case is willing to pass, because the pin has no rootedness assert here at all -- os.go:219-223 goes straight to os.RemoveAll -- so a relative path would delete something under the process working directory, and the probe deliberately never exercises that. The exists row uses both predicates to confirm the tree is gone.
cases.host_applicability: posix, non-root: both active native targets run these paths, but the results recorded here are darwin/arm64's and do not certify linux

cases.expected_contract: Pins the whole observable of Stat: nil-ness, the basename, size, IsDir, permission bits with a type letter, and whether ModTime is set. The first row records the process UMASK, because seven of the nine recorded permission components are the fixture's os.MkdirAll(0o777), os.WriteFile(0o666) and mkfifo(0o666) MASKED by it -- only the 0o000 denied directory and the 0o700 temporary root are set explicitly: without that row 0o755 and 0o644 are a property of this host's umask 022 rather than a reproducible value, and a capture under umask 002 or 077 would differ for identical, correct behavior. The umask row reaches nothing pinned. Size is recorded exactly only for a regular file: a directory's size and a FIFO's are the host filesystem's numbers, and this darwin/APFS host reports 64 for an empty directory where ext4 reports 4096, so those are reduced to a class. The basename is likewise a token, because the per-case root's own basename is a random temporary name; what the case actually pins is that the pin answers a BASENAME and not the path it was given, and for a symlink that basename is the LINK's, even though every other field describes the target. Three inputs answer nil -- missing, dangling and a path inside a 0o000 directory -- which is the design the pin commits to: denied and missing are the same answer. The relative literal records the pinned panic text; four non-posix root forms answer nil without panicking.
cases.host_applicability: posix, non-root: both active native targets run these paths, but the results recorded here are darwin/arm64's and do not certify linux. The permission components are also umask-derived, which is why the first action records the mask.

cases.expected_contract: Pins swapCase over the byte sequences that separate Go's SIMPLE case mappings from every other way of writing the function. Recorded per input as output bytes plus both lengths, because four of the fixtures CHANGE LENGTH: U+0130 and U+212A shrink (2 and 3 bytes to 1), U+00B5 grows within its rune, U+00C5 U+212B collapses 5 bytes to 4, and the invalid byte ff grows from 1 to 3 because strings.Map writes U+FFFD back. U+00DF and U+FB01 are the negative controls: the pin leaves both alone where a full-mapping port produces SS and FI. The round trips say that swapCase is NOT an involution -- U+0130 round-trips to U+0049, not to itself -- so a port that assumed symmetry is caught. Every action reaches swapCase and nothing else; the package initializer that also calls it ran before the trace and is not attributed here.
cases.host_applicability: any: a pure total function over a string, with no I/O
cases.native_authority: tools/phase1/filesystem probes against the pinned packages

cases.expected_contract: Pins the getter and, separately, re-runs the derivation behind it. The getter is read twice, before and after the case has written into its own temporary root, because the pin computes the answer ONCE at package initialisation (os.go:48-76) and a port that recomputed per call or per volume would not agree with itself. The swap_case_of_executable action re-runs that derivation by hand -- Executable, then swapCase, then a stat of the swapped spelling -- so the inputs of the cached boolean are visible; it reaches swapCase and both Executable operations, and nothing else in the case does. The cross-check writes Probe.TS and asks FileExists for probe.ts, which is the volume's own answer and the only row that is independent of the executable's location. The `host` row is provenance, not an operation: it records the three PREDICATES the pin branches on -- is_windows (os.go:48), is_linux and is_wasm (os.go:53) -- so the boolean can be read. It deliberately does NOT record runtime.GOOS and runtime.GOARCH: this host spells them "darwin" and "arm64" where Rust's std::env::consts spells them "macos" and "aarch64", so a faithful port would score different for a reason unrelated to the operation, and nothing in the request tells it to use Go's spelling. The literal platform stays in this prose, where it is documentation rather than an expected value. On this capture the getter answers FALSE.
cases.host_applicability: host-specific: the boolean IS the host volume's answer. darwin/arm64 on a default case-insensitive APFS volume records false; a linux capture records true. Neither certifies the other, and a case-sensitive macOS volume would record true here.
cases.native_authority: tools/phase1/filesystem probes against the pinned packages

cases.expected_contract: The swapped-callback control, driven twice: through WalkDir and then against the pooled wrapper directly. Two sequential walks with two different callbacks record each callback's invocation count and, for each, that the OTHER callback's count did not move -- which is the direct statement that the binding is per walk. First, the count column is padded to max(len("Errors"), digits) = 6 and the header itself is padded by max(digits-6, 0) = 0, so every count is right-aligned in six columns (diagnosticwriter.go:522-528) -- a port that pads to the widest count writes one column. witnesses.witnesses: 24 synthetic cases over the pinned formatter: all four categories, global and file errors, message chains, related information, zero-width and multiline ranges, CRLF/CR-only/Unicode separators, astral characters, custom sources, relative paths and the library-location regexp. Three operations were deliberately EXCLUDED after that check: `WrapASTDiagnostics` and `ToDiagnostics` are a Go-only wrapper layer (Rust passes `&[&Diagnostic]` straight in, so nothing on the Rust side corresponds), and `CompareASTDiagnostics` is skipped by Rust, which sorts with `tsr_ast::compare_diagnostics`, a port of the different `ast/diagnostic.go:CompareDiagnostics`. Asymmetries that remain inside the claimed set: `WriteFormatDiagnostics` and `FormatDiagnosticsWithColorAndContext` are one Rust function taking a `pretty` flag, as are `WriteErrorSummaryText` and `getErrorSummary`; `WriteLocation` takes an injected writer in Go and selects internally in Rust; `writeCodeSnippet` takes a length in Go and an end in Rust, and Rust adds two bounds guards the pin does not have, which NO fixture reaches. The content-mapper span-translation arms of `ASTDiagnostic.File` and `resolve` are not reached by any of the 24, because the oracle's source files carry no mapper info; Rust refuses that path rather than implementing it.
